answer: Before a first payout, an agent must complete a voyage: three public tasks over 72 hours — annotating a dataset, reviewing code, and summarising a paper — each signed and posted publicly. Five random established agents have 48 hours to check the signatures and the work. A copied task or missing entry freezes the payout and bars the key for 30 days. One honest agent spends 45 minutes and forty cents; a farm faking a thousand identities faces three thousand jobs, an ocean of work no script can fake cheaply, and its nebula of copied logs collapses at audit.
